kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: Why Trump just loosened the rules on 'dyed diesel' — normally a farm fuel
wire.summary: Trump is temporarily allowing this fuel to be used on highways, although it's typically just for off-road farm and construction vehicles. Could that lower the price of diesel?

wire.title: How Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has brought the culture wars to the military
wire.summary: The New York Times reporter Greg Jaffe says Hegseth has disproportionately blocked promotions of Black and women senior officers, and he's also been purging the military of transgender people.

wire.title: She got Trump's $500 check for health insurance. To her, it's a 'political stunt'
wire.summary: As checks from President Trump for health costs hit millions of mailboxes, a poll shows Americans don't trust Republicans on healthcare. Experts doubt it will move the needle and say it is likely illegal.

wire.title: Gut microbes followed migrating humans across continents, new study suggests
wire.summary: New research looks at the surprising similarities in the gut microbiomes of hunter-gathers in Tanzania and horticulturalists in Bolivia, and asks: What role do these bacteria play in human health?

wire.title: Greetings from Lahore, Pakistan, whose high court offers an oasis for chatter and chai
wire.summary: The Lahore High Court is a near-perfect specimen of British South Asian colonial architecture and its main square is a pleasant spot shaded by banyan trees.

wire.title: DIY fertilizer is a blessing as farmers face steep prices due to the Iran war
wire.summary: It's hard enough being a small-scale farmer. Then the Iran war drove up fertilizer prices. So farmers are using a traditional Asian recipe to make their own. They call it a "labor of love."

wire.title: U.S. moves long-range bombers from U.K. And, Israel allegedly warned before Oct. 7
wire.summary: A possible Iranian threat led the U.S. to remove long-range bombers from a U.K. base. And, Israelis are learning that their prime minister may have been warned before the Oct. 7 attacks.

wire.title: Who will win the 2026 Nobel Prize in economics?
wire.summary: A thinly traded prediction market offers a starting point. We explore potential winners and the big ideas that could earn them economics' biggest prize.

wire.title: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai win Nobel Prize in chemistry
wire.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry Wednesday for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

wire.title: Over 1,000 children are buried at juvenile detention centers nationwide
wire.summary: Researchers uncovered the graves of more than 1,000 children next to juvenile detention facilities in 29 states. At one Maryland gravesite, 230 Black boys are buried.

wire.title: France halts use of stun grenades after boy's hand blown off in student protests
wire.summary: The step comes after several groups complained of police using disproportionate force towards teenagers.

wire.title: Israelis demand accountability over 7 October failures three years after attacks
wire.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to take any personal responsibility for what happened or order a state inquiry.

wire.title: Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness
wire.summary: People with mental illness alone were to be eligible for assisted dying in Canada in March 2027, but that has now been paused indefinitely.

wire.title: Trump to speak to Putin about plague lab worker's death in Russia
wire.summary: Fears that the death may have been caused by pneumonic plague has prompted calls for more transparency from Russia.

wire.title: Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 19 in block of flats
wire.summary: Five children are among the victims of a strike that destroyed 30 flats in northern Ukraine as families slept.

wire.title: Sri Lanka's ex-first lady arrested over alleged misuse of children's hospital donations
wire.summary: The 73-year-old has been arrested over allegations that a charity she is linked to misused donations.
